text:
nora: Quick question — for rollout metadata, do we add an explicit `hydrate_on_rollout` field on pins, or rely on client-side probes/rehydration? Trying to balance correctness during fast canaries vs metadata size and churn.
alex: what's the targeted behavior? full KV warm vs just routing hints?
nora: Ideally short: if hydrate=true we force prefix-cache refresh/kv-warm on initial traffic for that tenant; false = lazy, rely on first requests to populate. Concern: forcing hydration spikes infra cost and can slow rollout.
ben: +1 on tradeoff. If we expose a boolean we make it easy for product but increasing surface area. Also telemetry/ops needs to know when hydration runs.
tara: telemetry concern: hydrated rollouts would create noisy token-level spikes. We have to tag traces w/ rollout_id and hydration=true. Don't want those metrics conflated with normal traffic.
javier: infra note: forcing hydrate means we either prefetch checkpoints or run synthetic requests. Both have different failure modes. Prefetch = heavy IO; synthetic = may not hit same shard patterns.
alex: maybe middle ground: three-state enum? `hydration: [off, async_prefetch, client_probe]` — off = lazy; async_prefetch = control-plane kicks off background warm; client_probe = clients call an endpoint to hydrate KV before routing real traffic.
nora: enum seems expressive but increases schema size. Any objections to compact encoding like `h=0|1|2`? :shrug:
ben: encoding compactly is fine internally, but keep human-readable in higher-level UI/CLI. Also need a clear failure contract: if prefetch fails, do we rollback or fall back to lazy? I vote fall back to lazy + alert.
tara: add telemetry tag `rollout.hydration` with values off/async/probe so we can filter. Also add `rollout.hydration_attempts` counter.
javier: ops implication: async_prefetch should be rate-limited per GPU pool and respect tenant quotas to avoid noisy neighbor. Must expose `/admin/hydration/status?rollout_id=...` for ops tooling.
alex: sample minimal pin shape for compatibility:
```
pin:
  model: gptx-3b
  variant: v2
  rollout_id: r-2026-03-23-42
  hydration: async_prefetch
```
nora: good. Also thinking of defaulting to `client_probe` for hosted free-tier and `async_prefetch` for enterprise Dedicated when they opt-in.
ben: one more: UX for rollbacks. If we mark as hydrated and then rollback, we need a way to mark caches as stale. Maybe a `dehydrate_on_rollback: true` flag? Or invert: hydration is idempotent if KV includes release_id.
tara: we already have release stamps on KV entries. Make hydration attach release_stamp; clients should ignore older stamps. So dehydrate isn't necessary if stamps are correct.
javier: final ops checklist: throttles, telemetry, admin endpoints, failure fallback to lazy, and per-tenant budget checks.
nora: ok action items: 1) add enum hydration field to pin schema (off/async_prefetch/client_probe), 2) add telemetry keys rollout.hydration and rollout.hydration_attempts, 3) admin endpoint for status, 4) document default policies by deployment type. Will draft RFC update.
deploy-bot: note — canary for pin-schema-v2 merged to staging at 3876543400 :rotating_light:
nora: thanks all — I'll post an RFC diff and ping ops for quota numbers. :thumbsup:
